extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers, meta-science researchers, and practitioners building/using datasets and models for automated analysis of peer reviews (e.g., people developing peer-review quality estimation or meta-review generation systems)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, annotating, and evaluating automatic systems that analyze peer-review texts (sentence-level annotations across multiple layers) and generate summaries/meta-reviews; includes tasks for classifying referred section/aspect/role/importance and for summarization/meta-review generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation layer — Referred article section (Task 1 labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels used to mark which section of the referred paper a reviewer statement refers to. Columns shown in tables: M, ABS, INT, RWK, PDI, DAT, MET, EXP, RES, ANA, TNF, FWK, BIB, EXT, OAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Task 1 annotation layer used for sentence-level classification. The paper reports label-wise F1 scores (micro-averaged) per label for different methods (see Table 6). Abbreviations appear in tables (e.g., ABS, INT) and are used as the canonical label tokens in the dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation layer — Referred aspect in article (Task 2 labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels that capture the specific aspect of the paper a reviewer sentence comments on. Columns shown in Task 2 tables: CLA, APR, NOV, SUB, IMP, CMP, PNF, REC, EMP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Task 2 in the benchmark. Performance is reported as label-wise (micro-averaged) F1 per label and overall accuracy per method (see Table 6 and Table 8). The abbreviations correspond to aspect categories in the annotation schema.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation layer — Role of the reviewer statement (Task 3 labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels describing the communicative role of a reviewer sentence (e.g., critique, suggestion, question, summary). Columns in Task 3 table: APC, CRT, DFT, DIS, FBK, QSN, SMY, SUG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task 3 evaluates classification of sentence roles. The paper reports per-label F1 scores and overall system accuracy for these roles (see Table 7 and Table 8). Role distinctions may overlap in practice (authors note fuzzy boundaries between some labels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation layer — Importance of reviewer content (Task 4 labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels capturing the importance or function of a sentence in review text (e.g., general comment vs. actionable major/minor points). Columns in Task 4 table include GEN, MAJ, MIN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task 4 is a classification problem to detect whether content is a general remark, a major comment, or a minor comment. Results are reported with label-wise F1 and overall accuracy (see Table 7 and Table 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review summarization objectives (Task 5 objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two summarization objectives: (1) generate a summary for each review and compare it with annotated major comments (gold standard); (2) generate a summary of the three reviews combined for a paper and compare it with the meta-review (area chair written gold standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both extractive (TextRank) and abstractive (Transformer encoder-decoder) baselines were used. Evaluation uses ROUGE metrics (R1, R2, R-L) and precision/recall/F1. The paper notes objective 2 is harder because meta-reviews are not simple summaries of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review generation required components
rubrics_metrics.description: A meta-review should encompass: a concise description of the submission’s main content, a concise summary of the reviewer’s discussion, and an explicit recommendation and justification on the fate of the paper (citing ICLR MetareviewGuide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes that meta-review generation is a challenging NLG task and requires summarization plus opinion synthesis. The ICLR MetareviewGuide is referenced for guidance on what meta-reviews should include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review auxiliary subtasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper states meta-review generation would require additional sub-capabilities: summarization, redundancy elimination, diversity estimation, and sentiment analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are presented as necessary components for successful automatic meta-review generation; the authors note that meta-reviews often include area-chair opinionation beyond simple aggregation of review content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for classification tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Label-wise F1 scores (micro-averaged) and overall accuracy figures are used to evaluate models on Tasks 1–4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables report per-label F1 (micro-averaged) for multiple baseline methods (TF-IDF+RF, BERT variants, etc.) and overall accuracy for each task. The paper also discusses when F1 is reported and suggests F1 is appropriate for imbalanced datasets (reviewer comment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for summarization (Task 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROUGE family metrics (R1 for unigram overlap, R2 for bigram overlap, R-L for longest common subsequence) and Precision, Recall, F1 are used to evaluate summarization outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 9 details R1, R2, R-L and P/R/F1 for TextRank (extractive) and Transformer (abstractive) baselines on per-review summarization and combined-review→meta-review summarization. The authors interpret lower scores for objective 2 as evidence meta-reviews require more than straightforward summarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLOS reviewer checklist / evaluation questions (example of a review rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five reviewer questions used by PLOS ONE as the review template: (1) Is the manuscript technically sound, and do the data support the conclusions? (2) Has the statistical analysis been performed appropriately and rigorously? (3) Have the authors made all data underlying the findings fully available? (4) Is the manuscript presented in intelligible fashion and written in standard English? (5) Review Comments to the Author (space to explain answers and provide additional concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit review criteria provided in the decision letter; they reflect an operational rubric reviewers are asked to follow when assessing manuscripts for PLOS ONE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript revision submission requirements (editorial procedural rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a revised manuscript: include a rebuttal letter responding to each point, a marked-up copy (track changes), and an unmarked final manuscript. Update any funding statement changes via cover letter/online form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is procedural guidance from the journal for producing a revision that meets editorial requirements; the decision letter lists these as mandatory items for revision submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical note on meta-review nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviews are not merely summaries; area chairs include opinionated views after reading reviews, hence automatic meta-review needs to synthesize opinions, not just extract reviewer content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation is used to explain why combined-review→meta-review summarization scores are lower and to motivate inclusion of sentiment/opinion modeling and synthesis in automatic approaches.
